title: The Premium Already Charged to a Travel Protection Plans Certificate
content:
The premium already charged to a Travel Protection Plans certificate, against which a re-rated premium is set, is read from the certificate's own premium record.

Where the certificate's premium lines carry a base premium and no premium has been returned on the certificate, the premium already charged is the total of its rating lines other than the policy fee.

Where the certificate's premium lines carry a base premium and premium has been returned on the certificate, the premium already charged is the net of those lines after the returns.

Where neither holds, the premium already charged is the figure the certificate records as premium paid.

## The three readings

| Base premium line on the certificate | Premium returned on the certificate | The premium already charged |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stands | None | The total of the certificate's rating lines, less the policy fee |
| Stands | Some amount returned | That same total after the returns have been netted off |
| Does not stand | Either way | The figure the certificate records as premium paid |

## Reading the record

The first two readings both require a base premium line to stand on the certificate; they are told apart by whether any premium has been returned on it. In both, the policy fee is taken out of the total, because the fee is not a rating line. In the second, the returns are then netted off what remains, so the figure follows what the policyholder has actually borne.

The third reading is reached whenever no base premium line stands on the certificate at all, and it rests on the certificate's own record of premium paid rather than on the individual lines.

Hypothetically, a certificate whose rating lines come to 465.00 USD including a policy fee of 15.00 USD, with nothing returned, has a premium already charged of 450.00 USD. Where 60.00 USD has since been returned on that certificate, the premium already charged is 390.00 USD. Where no base premium line stands at all, the figure is whatever the certificate records as premium paid.
